questions.text: 1.1. Judge the importance of time dimension when making a difference between the business case and the project charter. (2)
questions.correctAnswer: A business case is prepared before project authorization to justify feasibility and expected value. The project charter is created at initiation to formally authorize the project and the project manager. Their purpose and timing differ: business case supports the decision to invest; the charter authorizes the chosen project.

questions.text: 1.2. You recommend the adaptive life cycle as the most appropriate product life cycle to guide and facilitate the schedule management strategy. Justify your recommendation. (4)
questions.correctAnswer: An adaptive life cycle fits because requirements for the artist-booking/content-sales platform may develop as users and the team learn. Work can be prioritized and delivered in short increments, with regular demonstrations and stakeholder feedback used to refine requirements and the schedule. This supports change while producing useful functionality.

questions.text: 1.3.2. Activity C indicates that the project manager engages in identifying potential risks and risk reduction techniques to better the project’s chances of success. Predict five critical risks that are likely to occur in the development of this project. For each risk, recommend a technique to address it. (10)
questions.correctAnswer: Examples (any five distinct risk–response pairs): (1) Key developers resign or are overtasked → capacity planning, cross-training, realistic workload and retention incentives. (2) Unrealistic time/cost estimates → estimate with historical data and several-point estimates, then replan incrementally. (3) Wrong functionality or misunderstood artist/client needs → prototypes, requirements workshops and user validation. (4) Poor usability/interface → test wireframes and prototypes with artists and clients. (5) Scope changes disrupt the schedule → backlog prioritization and formal change control. (6) External platform/API integration fails → early integration spikes, vendor specifications, contracts and testing. (7) Technical difficulty building booking/content-sales services → feasibility prototype and targeted training.
aiRubric: Award up to 2 marks per distinct risk paired with a suitable mitigation, to a maximum of five pairs (10).
Risks should be plausible for a new e-commerce platform / team / artist-service context.
Mitigations should address the stated risk rather than merely restate it.
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Mark with the method shown in the key, while accepting equivalent valid wording, workings, units and sensible rounding. The reference answer is a study aid, not an official memorandum.
questions.explanation:
Risk identification is stronger when each risk has an actionable response. The supplied solutions discuss staffing, estimation, requirements, usability, change, external components and technical difficulty.

Student note: Use five different pairs; do not list five mitigations for the same risk.
questions.studentNote: Use five different pairs; do not list five mitigations for the same risk.

questions.text: 1.3.3. Activity D indicates that the service manager identifies preliminary human and physical resources. In resource management plan, the service manager expresses his concern about the resignation of two project team members who worked on the schedule management team, citing overtasking (specifically, questioning the need for a schedule management plan for each project management process group) and the absence of incentives to reward performance. To avoid further resignations, decide on an appropriate incentive plan for team members who work on the schedule management plan. (2)
questions.correctAnswer: Offer a fair, transparent team incentive for completing agreed schedule-management deliverables by the target date while meeting quality and workload expectations—for example, a small team bonus or recognition after an approved plan, with workload reviewed and no reward for rushed, low-quality work.
aiRubric: Propose a concrete reward/recognition plan tied to performance (1).
Include a fair condition such as on-time completion with quality/approved deliverable (1).
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Mark with the method shown in the key, while accepting equivalent valid wording, workings, units and sensible rounding. The reference answer is a study aid, not an official memorandum.
questions.explanation:
Incentives should reward useful performance rather than simply speed. Quality, realistic workload and clear criteria reduce pressure to cut corners.

Student note: Tie the reward to a measurable deliverable and protect quality.
questions.studentNote: Tie the reward to a measurable deliverable and protect quality.

questions.text: 1.3.4. Activity E indicates that project manager engages in financial analysis. Life cycle costing analysis indicates that it will take 1 year to complete the project, and that the system will be in place/active for a 1 year before a reduction in the number of TikTok artists subscribing for e-beats_Africa’s service occurs. Project Y costs R30,000 in Year 0 and increases by R1,000 a year through Year 4; projected income is R40,000, R48,000, R60,000 and R66,000 in Years 1–4. The paper describes a five-year subscription plan with Year 0 as the first cost year.

2.3. The project manager instructs you to use the ROI formula for multiyear projects to calculate the ROI for Project X and Project Y.

2.3.2. Use the ROI formula for multiyear projects to calculate the ROI for Project X and Project Y. (8)
aiRubric: Use discounted totals and correct ROI formula (2).
X numerator/net discounted benefit R38 241.10 and denominator R43 208.25 (2).
Y numerator R33 546.89 and denominator R132 643.95 (2).
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Mark with the method shown in the key, while accepting equivalent valid wording, workings, units and sensible rounding. The reference answer is a study aid, not an official memorandum.
questions.explanation:
Project X returns about R0.885 of net discounted value for each rand of discounted cost, or 88.5%. Project Y returns about 25.29%.

Student note: The supplied solution sheet prints about 0.9% and 0.3%; those omit the conversion from ratios 0.885 and 0.253 to percentages. The corrected percentages are 88.50% and 25.29%.

2.3.3. Based on the ROIs calculated in question 2.3.2, which project do you recommend for e-beats_Africa? Justify your answer. (2)
questions.correctAnswer: Recommend Project X because its multiyear ROI is higher (about 88.50% versus 25.29%). Both ROI values are positive.
